_about: Hand-curated findings that are not recomputed by build_facts_json.py (interpretive notes, manual checks, deposit history). build_facts_json.py deep-merges this file into facts.json last, so re-running the pipeline no longer drops them.

max_vs_p99_robustness_check.finding: anbh_derived_max is identical (21.0092 m) at every built-fraction threshold from >0 through >=0.05, i.e. built-fraction thresholding does not filter the cell(s) producing it, while anbh_derived_p99 is stable and much lower (8.21-10.69 m across the same thresholds). The max is therefore not a robust ceiling statistic; the manuscript reports p99 instead (Section 5.1).

source_cell_pixel_inspection.method: Raw 100 m AGBH/ANBH pixels queried directly from agbh_2018_v3.tif / anbh_2018_v3.tif via gdal_translate -projwin around the cell centroid (ad hoc investigation, not a scripted pipeline step).
source_cell_pixel_inspection.note: A small, adjacent-pixel block (not a single-pixel spike) shows genuinely elevated raw AGBH (up to 11.2 m) and ANBH (up to 26.5 m) values, concentrated over a small fraction of the cell -- consistent with either a real small tall structure or shoreline/water-adjacent retrieval noise (the cell sits at the edge of the generous Lake Volta bounding envelope used for this check); not distinguishable from this data alone. 8 of 177 cells nationally with derived ANBH > 12 m fall within a generous Lake Volta bounding envelope (lon -0.35 to 0.55, lat 6.15 to 8.65); most extreme cells elsewhere (e.g. near Obuasi, Tarkwa/Prestea) have much higher built fraction (8-51%) and plausibly reflect real mining/industrial infrastructure.

agbh_confound_finding.description: The AGBH-vs-ANBH comparisons in the typology (Section 5.5) and regression (Section 5.2) are not independent of the retrieval-floor claim they were cited as evidence for, because AGBH = ANBH x built_fraction_2018, and built_fraction_2018 correlates strongly with the built-coverage variables used elsewhere in the paper. Flagged by external technical review, verified directly against the n=296,668 sample before any manuscript text was changed.
agbh_confound_finding.implication: AGBHs higher typology diagonal concordance (89.8% vs 64.2%) and higher regression R2 (0.946 vs 0.235) are each partly mechanical (AGBH shares information with the variable it is compared/regressed against), not purely evidence of ANBHs retrieval floor. Unconfounded evidence for the retrieval floor: the pixel-level histogram (Section 5.1) and the near-flat median ANBH across typology classes (Section 5.5), both properties of ANBH alone. The cross-dataset correlation gap vs Open Buildings V3 (Section 5.6) also does not share this construction.
agbh_confound_finding.fix_applied: Section 5.2, Section 5.5 (both paragraphs), Section 6.4 (new Limitation 2), Abstract, and paper2_response_to_reviewers_v3.md all restate this explicitly. No computed statistics changed -- this is a correction to interpretation/independence claims, not to the underlying numbers.

predictor_profile_reviewer2_major6.description: Section 4.7 regression predictors (built_coverage_2010, growth_1975_2010, growth_2010_2015, distance_to_nearest_cbd_m), by typology class -- added in response to a gap flagged in paper2_response_to_reviewers_v3.md (Reviewer #2, Major 6): this comparison existed in the prior AGBH-based revision but had not been carried into the ANBH-based rebuild.
predictor_profile_reviewer2_major6.headline_finding: High height / High prior expansion cells have built_coverage_2010 roughly 4-40x every other class (0.0534 vs 0.0002-0.0141) and the shortest mean distance to the nearest CBD (61.9 km vs 70.2-75.0 km), on predictors the typology was not constructed from -- an independent check that the classification captures a real pattern.

table6_not_independent.description: Table 6 (Section 4.7 predictors by typology class) was originally described as an independent check on the typology. growth_1975_2010 + growth_2010_2015 sum EXACTLY to growth_1975_2015 (the typology horizontal axis) by construction -- not independent, arithmetically part of it. built_coverage_2010 correlates r=0.97 with 2018 built fraction (see agbh_confound_finding above) -- also not a clean independent check. Only distance_to_nearest_cbd_m is genuinely external to the typology construction.
table6_not_independent.fix_applied: Reframed as a descriptive class profile; independence claim removed except for CBD distance specifically (Section 5.5).

illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.description: A small, non-random illustration of the 120-cell manual-validation infrastructure, done in response to external review flagging that no validation had actually been completed. Not a substitute for the full protocol -- see caveats below.
illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.method: For each of the 3 region tiers (Metro_core, Periurban_corridor, Secondary_city), the single cell with the highest cell_anbh_derived_m (within the HighANBH stratum) and the single cell with the lowest (within the LowANBH stratum) were located via lat/lon centroid and viewed in Google Maps satellite imagery.

cells_checked.observation: Dense administrative/government core: Accra Metropolitan Assembly, ministry buildings, Ghana Revenue Authority HQ. Consistent with High height / High prior expansion.
Forested/rural land on Kumasi periphery, a handful of small scattered structures visible. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.

Dense peri-urban residential/commercial settlement (Kasoa-Ofaakor), predominantly low-rise. Consistent with High height / High prior expansion, though visually low-rise rather than tall -- appropriately, since High is relative to other peri-urban cells, not to the metro core.
Farmland, no visible structures in frame. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.
Dense institutional campus (Takoradi Technical University and surrounding hostels/services). Consistent with High height / High prior expansion.
Dense forest, no visible structures. Consistent with Low height / Low prior expansion.

illustrative_satellite_check_6_cells.result: 6 of 6 cells show the expected pattern (face validity holds for the most extreme, most confident classification cases).
caveats: Non-random: deliberately picked the most extreme cell per stratum, not a random draw -- says nothing about accuracy in the moderate/ambiguous cases where classification error actually matters.

Overhead-only imagery cannot distinguish a genuinely tall building from many low-rise buildings packed densely together, i.e. cannot independently verify the AGBH/ANBH distinction this paper is about.
No shadow-length, oblique, or street-level imagery was used, so no storey count or height estimate was attempted -- only a coarse built-density/land-use impression.
114 of the 120-cell sample and the storey-count coding field remain uncompleted.

Fixes: marker-overplotting artefacts in dense urban cores, no country outline (blank cells were indistinguishable from outside Ghana), no scale bar/north arrow, and axes plotted in raw unprojected degrees.
added_elements: National boundary overlay (GADM gadm41_GHA.gpkg, ADM_ADM_0 layer)
Scale bar (manual, sized to ~20% of map width, rounded to a nice km value)
gis_review_fixes.disclosure_fix: Fig. 1 (ANBH map) already disclosed N and the colour-scale percentile cap; Fig. 2 (AGBH map) did not. Both now disclose N, the cap value, and CRS consistently, and both explicitly flag that their N (296,677, cells with valid GHSL height data) is 9 more than the n=296,668 regression/typology sample, which additionally requires non-missing 1975/2010/2015 built-coverage covariates not needed for a univariate height map.
gis_review_fixes.caption_fix: Manuscript Fig. 1 caption originally named only Accra-Tema, Kumasi, and Tamale as visual peaks. A small number of mining centres (e.g. Obuasi) show comparably strong localized ANBH signal and are not among the 15 named study regions; the caption now says so explicitly, with a caveat that this plausibly reflects industrial rather than residential/commercial structures.

reproducibility_deposit_expansion.description: The GitHub deposit (github.com/dzimike/Urban-growth-pathways-) was expanded to include the upstream pipeline (scripts/01_setup_project.py through scripts/09_aggregate_to_grid.py, plus 03b_generate_250m_grid.py, and environment.yml), previously described in words only, not deposited.
checks_performed_before_deposit: Grepped all 10 scripts for api_key/secret/password/token/credential/access_key patterns -- none found.
Grepped for hard-coded /Users/... absolute paths -- none found (all use config.py, same pattern as scripts/revision_v3/).

Confirmed no Earth Engine authentication calls (import ee / ee.Initialize / ee.Authenticate) in any of the 10 scripts, despite environment.yml declaring earthengine-api as a project dependency for other, non-deposited parts of the wider project.
py_compile syntax check on all 10 files -- all valid.
still_not_reproducible_without: The raw third-party datasets (GHSL, Open Buildings V3/2.5D Temporal, Overture, OSM, WorldPop, Ghana PHC, GADM, DEM/terrain, night-lights) -- licensing prevents redistribution.

A working install of the upstream conda environment (environment.yml, python=3.11 with rasterio/fiona/full GDAL bindings) -- not re-verified in the environment this v3 revision was prepared in, which lacks system GDAL/rasterio (see pixel_validation/aggregation notes elsewhere in this file and audit_report.md Section 6). This is a pre-existing, already-disclosed environment gap, not something introduced by this deposit.
